steps.message:
I fixed an infinite loop in `rich/cells.py` within the `split_graphemes` function. The loop occurred when a string started with a zero-width character that was not in the `SPECIAL` set, as the `index` was not being incremented when `spans` was empty. I added a fallback `else` block to ensure `index` is incremented in this case.

To verify, you can add a test case to `tests/test_cells.py` that calls `split_graphemes` with a string starting with a zero-width character (e.g., `\u200b`).

steps.message: The fix addresses an infinite loop in `split_graphemes` by ensuring that the loop index is incremented when a zero-width character is encountered at the beginning of a string. I verified the fix by testing it with leading zero-width characters, which now correctly advance the index instead of looping infinitely.
